sections.content: How many people are "building and civil engineering technicians"?

11,530 people

were counted on the census as "building and civil engineering technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Building and civil engineering technicians perform a variety of technical support functions to assist civil and building engineers.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "building and civil engineering technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "building and civil engineering technicians", 13.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "building and civil engineering technicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "building and civil engineering technicians" included:

  • financial administrative occupations (other)
  • mechanical engineers
  • rail construction and maintenance operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "building and civil engineering technicians" there were more men than women (75.1% compared with 24.9%).

This means "building and civil engineering technicians" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, engineering and technology associate professionals".

Men made up 75.1% and women made up 24.9% of "building and civil engineering technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "building and civil engineering technicians" included:

  • science, engineering and production technicians (other)
  • IT managers
  • fishmongers and poultry dressers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "building and civil engineering technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "building and civil engineering technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "building and civil engineering technicians", 7.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (88.7% compared with 11.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (82.9%) than self-employed (17.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
